title: EU SEMICeu Core Vocabularies
usedFor: EU public-sector canonical models — conformity (CCCEV), legal entities (Core Business Vocabulary). The natural anchor for operator identity and conformity assertions.
licence: CC-BY 4.0 for the current releases — confirmed 2026-08-11 directly from each vocabulary's own repository (`github.com/SEMICeu/CCCEV`, `github.com/SEMICeu/Core-Business-Vocabulary`), not a survey. Caveat: pre-2.0 CCCEV releases carried the ISA Open Metadata Licence v1.1 instead — re-check the licence of any specific older version/IRI before relying on CC-BY retroactively.
source: https://semiceu.github.io/CCCEV/ (Core Criterion and Core Evidence Vocabulary, v2.1.0, SEMIC Candidate Recommendation 2026-05-12) and https://semiceu.github.io/Core-Business-Vocabulary/ (v2.3.0, released 2026-05-12) — fetched and read directly.
finding: Two distinct vocabularies under this one entry, not one. **CCCEV**'s Criterion/Requirement/Evidence triad is shaped for public-procurement conformity checks — it does not map cleanly onto ESPR's declaration-of-conformity shape (confirmed against CIRPASS-2's own `COMP` module, which models `EUDeclarationOfConformity`/`ConformityCertificate`/`HarmonisedStandard` in ESPR-native terms instead). **Core Business Vocabulary**'s `LegalEntity` (legalName, registeredAddress, activity, companyType) maps much more directly onto an economic-operator/facility identity block. Checked IR (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 12's semantic repository for a textual SEMIC tie — fetched the regulation directly and searched for 'SEMIC', 'Core Vocabularies', 'CCCEV', 'Core Business Vocabulary': zero matches. Art. 11(2)'s permissive language ('may build on existing Union semantic assets') names nothing specific, and no Commission registry page found names SEMIC either. One real but different-layer tie does exist: Art. 12(3) requires the registry's dataset *metadata* to conform to DCAT-AP, itself a SEMIC deliverable — governs metadata-about-datasets, not the DPP attribute semantics layer. **Re-checked 2026-10-13:** the CCCEV page now states "The current version of the CCCEV is 2.2.0" and describes the specification as under development by the Working Group, and GitHub's release list shows v2.2.0 published 2026-05-12 and v2.1.0 published 2024-10-08. The Core Business Vocabulary page states that its current version is 2.3.0, and its GitHub release v2.3.0 is dated 2026-06-09. So the "v2.1.0, Candidate Recommendation 2026-05-12" recorded above for CCCEV matches neither the page nor the releases, and 2026-05-12 is not the release date of Core Business v2.3.0. Neither repository has a LICENSE file, which is why GitHub reports no licence. Each README states "Copyright © 2026 European Union. All material in this repository is published under the licence CC-BY 4.0, unless explicitly otherwise mentioned", so the licence finding above stands, on the README's wording. The pre-2.0 caveat stands.
nextStep: Map Core Business Vocabulary's legal-entity terms — or at minimum its property names as a semanticId prefix — for the operator/facility identity block; Commission authorship gives it more regulatory legitimacy than any alternative and the shape fits. CCCEV stays gap-source only: read it for missing evidence-typing concepts, never adopt its IRIs, since its procurement shape doesn't fit ESPR conformity data.
